solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This is how spies left informal gathering

blocks.note: 'so' means 'in this way'
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An account of how a group of spies slipped away from a casual get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words read like part of the story but they are just a two-letter word meaning 'thus'.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a party or friendly get-together, typically one run by a club or church.

clue.text: A little insult angers sovereign

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A minor slight provokes the monarch's fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside inSULT ANgers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the ruler of a Muslim state, so a sovereign by title.

clue.text: Primrose in part of animal's mouth

blocks.note: a cow is the animal, with its possessive
a lip is part of the mouth

explanation.surface: A wild flower found stuck in a grazing animal's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'a cow's lip'; the apostrophe is kept in the reading, dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild plant of the primrose family, Primula veris, with yellow flowers.

clue.text: With gold, artist creates special atmosphere

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter uses gilding to give a picture a distinctive mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive feeling or quality that seems to surround a person or place.

clue.text: Peer is said to be childless

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the spelling may change

blocks.note: a baron is a peer, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: Gossip that a certain lord has no heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren describes a person or animal unable to have offspring, an old word for infertile.

clue.text: Scotsman unfortunately died before broadcast

blocks.note: 'alas' is an expression of regret
d. is the abbreviation for died
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A man from Scotland sadly passed away before his programme went out.
explanation.walkthrough: Alasdair is a Scottish form of Alexander, so a typical Scots name stands in for the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Alasdair is a characteristically Scottish given name, so it can stand for a Scotsman.

clue.text: Engineers manage a repeat broadcast

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Technicians arrange for a programme to be shown again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a showing again of a television series or film that has already been aired.

clue.text: Fresh flood defence for Notts town

blocks.note: fresh means new
Noah's ark was the defence against the biblical Flood

explanation.surface: A new barrier against rising water is planned for a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English county; Newark-on-Trent is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark is a market town on the River Trent in Nottinghamshire, England.

clue.text: Undemanding hilltop not very high

blocks.note: low is the opposite of high
the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: A description of an easy walk up a modest summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read as 'a hilltop that is not very high', so the second phrase comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowbrow culture is unsophisticated and makes few intellectual demands on its audience.

clue.text: Suffered from exposure, but survived

blocks.note: first meaning: worn by wind, rain and sun
second meaning: came safely through a difficult period

explanation.surface: Someone caught out in the cold had a bad time but lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Weathered means both worn by the elements and having come through a crisis, as in weathering a storm.

clue.text: An argument about River Dart

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so one word wraps the next letter

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a row is a quarrel
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A dispute concerning the River Dart, which flows through Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D makes Dart look like the Devon river; it is the definition, a missile, and the river is a separate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart and an arrow are both small pointed missiles shot or thrown at a target.

clue.text: Take side off piece of furniture to make it fit

indicators.note: removing a side means cutting off an edge, here the opening letter

blocks.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Instructions for removing a panel so a cabinet will fit a space.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fit for something is to be able, capable or competent to do it.

clue.text: One that forgives a tale-teller

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who excuses an offence
second meaning: one of Chaucer's pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tale-teller' suggests a liar, but it points to Chaucer, whose Pardoner tells one of the Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardoner grants forgiveness; the medieval Pardoner sold indulgences and narrates a tale in Chaucer's poem.

clue.text: Assisting girl with jewellery

blocks.note: Ena is a girl's name, a crossword stock name
bling is slang for showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Helping a young woman put on her necklaces and rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Enabling means making something possible for someone, a way of helping them.

clue.text: Believer is quiet and strangely hesitant

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd way, so the following word is mixed up

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A person of faith is subdued and oddly unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist holds that God is identical with the universe and nature, so is a kind of religious believer.

clue.text: Time to pay for freedom in the bar

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a ransom is money paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: A kidnap story: the moment arrives to hand over money in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a crossbar in a window or door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, especially one above a door or across a window.

clue.text: With a cutting edge, youth pierces couch

indicators.note: to pierce is to go into something, so one word is pushed inside another

blocks.note: a couch can be a bed
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young man armed with a knife stabs the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bladed is fitted with a blade, a flat sharpened cutting part.

clue.text: Covering small area of unproductive land

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a heath is open uncultivated land

explanation.surface: Vegetation spreading over a little patch of poor ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover or case, such as one for a blade.

clue.text: Spotted insect and hen, may one say?

blocks.note: first meaning: the red beetle with black spots
second meaning, playful: a female bird

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, splitting the word into 'lady' and 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is the British name for the ladybug beetle, and a hen is literally a female bird.

clue.text: Ledger entry's extremely defective part

indicators.note: 'extremely' points to the extremes of a word, its first and final letters

blocks.note: the two end letters of the word
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: An accountant complains that a book entry is badly wrong in places.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an entry in an account recording a sum owed or paid out.

clue.text: Mince remains hot to start with

indicators.note: only what comes at the start of the word is wanted, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Leftover minced meat is still warm at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the residue of a fire, placed after the starting letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped or minced meat, often leftover meat recooked.

clue.text: Leaving word poor quality stuff is at start of auction

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: tat is cheap, shoddy goods
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dealer's verdict that junk is being sold early in the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye when departing.

clue.text: A friend from America returning by one Muslim country

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the article plus bud, American slang for a friend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American pal comes back with someone else from an Islamic state.
explanation.walkthrough: Dubai is strictly an emirate within the UAE, loosely called a country here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a Gulf emirate whose state religion is Islam, a constituent state of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Where Dad can swim with ease?

definitions.text: Where Dad can swim with ease?

indicators.note: letters that swim move about freely, so their order is changed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about the place a non-swimming father could float effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the very salty water is so buoyant that anyone floats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea, a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, is so dense with salt that bathers float easily.

clue.text: Foolish time to put identifying mark into deer

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside, as 'into' confirms

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer
a tag is a label that identifies

explanation.surface: A daft moment when someone tries to brand a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of old age when the mind weakens, a time of senile foolishness.

clue.text: Heat of battle at mountain height

blocks.note: war is armed battle
Mt is the abbreviation for mountain or mount
h is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: The fierce heat of combat high in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat of battle' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is a moderate degree of heat, the quality of being warm.
